title: GPU OOM + CUDA driver mismatch debug notes - Liam Chen
content:
Summary:
- Intermittent CUDA OOMs observed on 4xA100-large machines while serving long-chat sessions (seq_len ~ 2048, batching enabled).
- Some runs show an explicit driver/runtime mismatch error (\"CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime\") on startup of containerized model server.
- Hypothesis: mixed causes — primarily driver vs runtime mismatch across host/container (NVIDIA driver older than CUDA runtime used by PyTorch), plus memory fragmentation / KV cache growth in long-lived processes.

Environment snapshot (collected at 2024-11-12 09:40 UTC):
- Host: ubuntu 20.04, kernel 5.15.0-58-generic
- GPU: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (4 cards)
- Driver (host): 470.57.02 (installed via apt from nvidia-driver-470)
- CUDA toolkit on host: /usr/local/cuda-11.8 (nvcc --version shows 11.8.120)
- Container base: nvidia/cuda:11.7.1-cudnn8-runtime-ubuntu20.04
- Torch in container: torch==2.0.1+cu117 (pip show)
- torchvision: 0.15.2+cu117

Commands I ran and outputs (important bits):
1) nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (UUID: GPU-xxxxx)
GPU 1: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (UUID: GPU-xxxxx)
...

2) nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv
name, driver_version, memory.total [MiB], memory.used [MiB]
NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB, 470.57.02, 40960 MiB, 1200 MiB

3) nvcc --version (inside container)
nvcc: NVIDIA (R) Cuda compiler driver
Copyright (c) 2005-2022 NVIDIA Corporation
Built on Wed_Oct_12_21:09:46_PDT_2022
Cuda compilation tools, release 11.7, V11.7.64

4) python snippet (inside container):
>>> import torch
>>> torch.cuda.is_available()
True
>>> torch.version.cuda
'11.7'
>>> torch.backends.cudnn.version()
8600

5) ldd of libtorch_cuda.so (inside container) -> showed a mismatch for libcuda.so.1 linking to /usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64/libcuda.so.1 (from host-mounted drivers) vs container's expectation. (logged full output into /tmp/ldd-libtorch.txt)

6) Reproduced error snippet from model server logs (trimmed):
2024-11-12T09:23:45.123Z ERROR: runtime init failed: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/server.py", line 214, in <module>
    model = load_model(...).to(device)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/torch/cuda/__init__.py", line 217, in _lazy_init
    torch._C._cuda_init()
RuntimeError: CUDA error: driver shutting down

7) Another run produced an OOM during inference (different session):
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.25 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 2.10 GiB already allocated; 30.50 GiB free; 1.25 GiB requested; ...)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/torch/cuda/memory.py", line 163, in _lazy_call
    ...

Notes from dmesg (host) around the time of driver error:
[Nov12 09:23:44] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[Nov12 09:23:44] NVRM: GPU at 00000000:00:1 failed with error 4

Actions tried so far (ordered rough):
- Restarted docker daemon + nvidia-container-runtime (systemctl restart docker nvidia-docker) -> transiently fixed one pod but error recurred.
- Rebooted host -> after reboot some containers started fine, but later same driver mismatch happened on another node.
- Ensured container runtime uses host driver (nvidia-container-toolkit) by mounting /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 into container and checking ldd -> confirmed container picks up host libcuda.so.1.
- Switched container base to nvidia/cuda:11.8-cudnn8-runtime -> reduced frequency of mismatches but still occasional OOMs in long-lived processes.
- Forced torch to use CUDA 11.7 wheels (torch==2.0.1+cu117) to match container base (11.7) — still saw driver errors when host driver older than toolkit used by other nodes.
- Added robust worker restart: when server fails with driver init error, orchestrator restarts container. This reduces customer impact but doesn't fix root cause.
- Reproduced memory growth locally with a simple script that keeps appending to kv cache (simulated long chat). Observed memory fragmenting and not releasing due to retained tensors on server side (possible ref leak).

Hypotheses / root cause candidates:
1) Driver/runtime mismatch between host driver and CUDA runtime used by PyTorch (container). Host driver 470 supports CUDA up to 11.4/11.5? Need to check compatibility matrix — likely driver is too old for some cu117 runtime bits. This explains "driver insufficient" errors.
2) Intermittent NVIDIA Xid errors (GPU fallen off the bus) pointing to hardware/PCIe issues or thermal/soft-reset events; when Xid occurs, driver can get into weird state and subsequent containers see driver init errors.
3) Memory fragmentation / retained tensors in long-lived server causing effective OOM even if aggregated free memory looks sufficient. Fragmentation + large allocations (KV caches) triggers OOM.
4) Mismatch between libcuda ABI exposed to container vs what torch expects (ldd showed different libcuda link targets) — race when host has multiple CUDA installs (11.8) but container expects 11.7. Symptom: linking to host libcuda but runtime symbols missing.

Immediate recommended mitigations (short-term):
- Standardize on host driver >= 510 (or the minimum recommended for CUDA 11.7/11.8/11.9) across the fleet. Create a rolling upgrade plan for driver to 515+ and validate with smoke tests.
- Pin container bases and torch wheels to matched CUDA (e.g., container nvidia/cuda:11.7 + torch+cu117) OR use CPU-backed warmup to avoid early GPU init mismatches.
- Add proactive health-check: on container start, run a lightweight torch.cuda.init() check and if it fails with driver mismatch, report node as unhealthy and avoid scheduling more pods there.
- For long-lived processes, add memory watchdog that dumps top tensors (torch.cuda.memory_summary(), objgraph) when memory high and triggers graceful restart if leak suspected.
- Reduce default batch sizes / use dynamic batching with hard caps to reduce peak allocations.

Longer-term actions / TODOs:
- (Ops) Create a driver-compatibility matrix doc and fleet rollout runbook. Linked JIRA: JIRA-RT-987.
- (Eng) Add better tensor retention instrumentation in model server: track per-request allocations with weakrefs, leak detector.
- (Infra) Validate PCIe/firmware on nodes that log Xid 79 — involve hardware team for nodes with repeated XID.
- (SRE) Add automated detection for "GPU has fallen off the bus" in host dmesg/metrics and cordon nodes automatically for investigation.
- (QA) Build a stress test that simulates long chat sessions and runs for 24+ hours to catch fragmentation/leak patterns.

Notes / breadcrumbs for future debugging:
- When I saw "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime" the stack trace pointed to torch._C._cuda_init(). This is almost always host driver < runtime mismatch. Fixing container alone sometimes masked the issue because some nodes had newer drivers.
- There are at least two distinct failure modes here: a) initialization failure (driver incompatible), b) runtime OOM (fragmentation/leak). Treat them separately in the runbook.
- Keep a copy of /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and dmesg around the time of failure. XID codes (79, 31, etc.) are useful to triage hardware vs software.

Quick repro script I used locally (trimmed):
# repro_kv_growth.py
import torch, time
model = torch.nn.Linear(1024, 1024).cuda()
kv = []
for i in range(10000):
    x = torch.randn(4, 1024, device='cuda')
    out = model(x)
    kv.append(out.detach())  # simulate retained cache -> memory grows
    if i % 100 == 0:
        print(i, torch.cuda.memory_allocated()/1024**2)
    time.sleep(0.01)

Observed behaviour: memory increased steadily and didn't free until process exit. Indicates retention rather than true allocator leak (but fragmentation likely afterwards).

Log pointers:
- /var/log/syslog and dmesg around 2024-11-12 09:23:40-09:24:00 (Xid 79)
- Model server logs: /var/log/model-server/2024-11-12.err.log (attached to JIRA)

Next immediate steps I will take (short checklist):
- [ ] Coordinate with infra to bump driver to 515 on one canary rack and run smoke tests. (Pinged Raja)
- [ ] Add start-up cuda sanity check to server image and fail fast if driver mismatch. (I'll draft a small PR)
- [ ] Implement a short-lived memory watchdog to capture summaries on OOM and force restart if leak suspected. (Prototype today)
- [ ] Run the 24h chat stress test on canary to reproduce fragmentation pattern.

If anyone has seen an "insufficient driver" message with host driver 470 and container/runtime 11.7/11.8 please ping here — curious if 470 occasionally works due to backwards compatibility or if we've just been lucky before.

References and quick links:
- NVIDIA compatibility docs: https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/cuda-compatibility/index.html
- Internal runbook: https://confluence.internal/redwood/gpu-debug-playbook
- JIRA: JIRA-RT-987

Notes to self: keep this doc chronological; append timestamps when re-checking. Save any patched containers and exact wheel filenames used for repro.
